items.title: feat: Propagate underlying MPT flags to vault shares
items.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Implements MPT flag governance for Single Asset Vault (SAV) and the Lending Protocol so that issuer changes to `lsfMPTCanTransfer` / `lsfMPTCanTrade` on an MPT underlying a vault behave consistently across vault deposits, withdrawals, P2P share payments, DEX offers, AMM placements, and offer crossing.

All behavioral changes are amendment-gated under `fixCleanup3_2_0`.

### Context of Change

The spec required three things:

1. **Block new exposure** when the issuer clears `lsfMPTCanTransfer` / `lsfMPTCanTrade`.
2. **Always allow recovery** so depositors are never trapped.
3. **Propagate transferability/tradability from the underlying to the vault share** so peer-to-peer share payments, DEX placements, AMM placements, and offer crossing inherit the issuer's restrictions.

#### 1. Recovery paths

`VaultWithdraw` and `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` call `canTransfer` between two pseudo-accounts (neither of which is the asset issuer), so the existing issuer carveout did not apply and withdrawals would fail with `tecNO_AUTH` after the issuer cleared `lsfMPTCanTransfer`.

A new `WaiveMPTCanTransfer` enum is threaded through `canTransfer`'s MPT and `Asset` overloads (default `No`, preserving every other call site). `VaultWithdraw` and `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` pass `Yes`, gated on the amendment. Other transferability checks (IOU NoRipple, freeze, requireAuth) still apply.

#### 2. Vault share inheritance via `sfReferenceHolding`

A new optional `UINT256` field on `MPTokenIssuance` points to the vault pseudo-account's holding for the underlying: the `MPToken` keylet for an MPT-backed vault, or the `RippleState` keylet for an IOU-backed vault. XRP-backed vaults leave the field unset.

- `VaultCreate` populates the field at share-issuance creation. `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` validates the pointed-to SLE exists and is of an expected type (`ltMPTOKEN` or `ltRIPPLE_STATE`).
- `canTransfer(MPTIssue, ...)`, `canTrade(Asset)`, `isVaultPseudoAccountFrozen`, and `checkMPTAllowed` (AMM / Offer-crossing / Check) read `sfReferenceHolding`, fetch the holding SLE via `keylet::unchecked`, derive the underlying via a new `assetOfHolding` helper, and dispatch the same check recursively.
- Recursion is bounded at `kMAX_ASSET_CHECK_DEPTH` (vault-of-vault-shares is already forbidden at `VaultCreate`; the cap is defensive). The bound and bookkeeping live inside the amendment-gated branch and are dead code pre-amendment.
- The recovery-path waive short-circuits inheritance: callers operate on the vault's direct underlying, never on a share, so skipping the branch honors the recovery intent without transitively unlocking a deeper underlying. The recursive call always passes `WaiveMPTCanTransfer::No`.

#### 3. Invariant

`ValidMPTIssuance` enforces, post-`fixCleanup3_2_0`:

- `sfReferenceHolding` may only be set on creation, only by `VaultCreate`.
- `sfReferenceHolding` is immutable on an existing `MPTokenIssuance`.
- Any `MPToken` / `RippleState` whose owner is a vault pseudo-account (account SLE has `sfVaultID`) may only be deleted by `VaultDelete`.

`visitEntry` bookkeeping is itself amendment-gated via the thread-local `isFeatureEnabled(fixCleanup3_2_0)` so pre-amendment transactions skip the new work entirely.

### API Impact

- [x] `libxrpl` change — new `sfReferenceHolding` field on `MPTokenIssuance`; new `WaiveMPTCanTransfer` enum; new `assetOfHolding` helper.

No public API or peer-protocol changes. All behavior gated under `fixCleanup3_2_0`.

## Test Plan

Covered in `Vault_test`, `Loan_test`, and `Invariants_test`:

- `sfReferenceHolding` writer correctness — populated by `VaultCreate` for MPT/IOU underlyings, unset for XRP, absent pre-amendment, absent for plain `MPTokenIssuanceCreate`.
- Recovery paths — post-amendment `VaultWithdraw` / `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` succeed after issuer clears `lsfMPTCanTransfer`; pre-amendment regression confirms historical failure mode.
- Share inheritance — P2P share Payment and IOU `NoRipple` propagation through `canTransfer`; DEX offers blocked through `canTrade`; AMM creation with shares blocked through `checkMPTAllowed` when the underlying `CanTrade` is cleared.
- Holding-deletion probes — full-balance `Clawback`, issuer-driven `Unauthorize`, `MPTokenIssuanceDestroy`, `TrustSet limit=0` all blocked against vault pseudo holdings; `VaultDelete` confirmed as the legitimate deletion path.
- Invariant violations — both field-misuse arms (set outside `VaultCreate`, mutation) and the holding-deletion rule.

## Future Tasks

- Back-port mechanism for vault shares created before `fixCleanup3_2_0` activated (currently exempt from inheritance).

items.title: refactor: Rename (mostly keylet) functions to more closely match the docs
items.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

As the title says, this PR renames a bunch of functions (mostly keylet functions) to match what the docs refer to these as, so that it's easier to know what function to use when you want to use a specific keylet.

Full list of renames:
- `keylet::line` -> `keylet::rippleState`
- `keylet::fees` -> `keylet::feeSettings`
- `keylet::signers` -> `keylet::signerList`
- `keylet::payChan` -> `keylet::payChannel`
- `keylet::nftpage` -> `keylet::nftokenPage`
- `keylet::nftoffer` -> `keylet::nftokenOffer`
- `keylet::mptIssuance` -> `keylet::mptokenIssuance`
- `keylet::loanbroker` -> `keylet::loanBroker`
- NFT serial -> NFT sequence

There are no functionality changes in this PR, only renames (and resulting linter changes).

### Context of Change

Repo cleanup

### API Impact

N/A, these are all internal names

items.title: fix: Remove non-canonical fields from `tx_json` in API v3
items.body:
In API v2, `tx` and `account_tx` responses include server-added lower-case fields (`date`, `ledger_index`, `ctid`) inside `tx_json` alongside canonical PascalCase transaction fields. In API v3, these fields must only appear at the top-level result object — a TODO in `Transaction.cpp` already noted this gap.

## High Level Overview of Change

For API v3, `tx_json` now contains only canonical signed transaction fields. Server-added metadata fields (`date`, `ledger_index`, `ctid`) are moved out of `tx_json` and appear exclusively at the top-level result object.

**Before (API v3, broken):**
```json
{
  "result": {
    "ledger_index": 3885449,
    "tx_json": {
      "Account": "r...",
      "TransactionType": "Payment",
      "date": 804007520,
      "ledger_index": 3885449
    }
  }
}
```

**After (API v3, fixed):**
```json
{
  "result": {
    "date": 804007520,
    "ledger_index": 3885449,
    "tx_json": {
      "Account": "r...",
      "TransactionType": "Payment"
    }
  }
}
```

API v2 behavior is unchanged.

### Context of Change

`Transaction::getJson` unconditionally added `ledger_index`, `date`, and `ctid` to the returned JSON. A TODO comment explicitly called for a `disable_API_prior_V3` flag to suppress these fields. This PR implements that fix, ensuring the fields are moved to the result level rather than dropped entirely.

### Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Tests (you added tests for code that already exists, or your new feature included in this PR)
- [x] Documentation update

### API Impact

- [x] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)

## Changes

- **`include/xrpl/protocol/STBase.h`**: Added `disable_API_prior_V3 = 0b0000'0100` to `JsonOptions`; updated `_all` mask accordingly.
- **`src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/Transaction.cpp`**: Wrapped `ledger_index`, `date`, and `ctid` injection in `if (!(options & JsonOptions::disable_API_prior_V3))` — implements the existing TODO.
- **`src/xrpld/rpc/handlers/Tx.cpp`**: API v3+ uses `disable_API_prior_V2 | disable_API_prior_V3`; API v2 retains `include_date | disable_API_prior_V2`. For API v3+, `date` is explicitly added at the result level from `result.closeTime`.
- **`src/xrpld/rpc/handlers/AccountTx.cpp`**: Same versioned options as `Tx.cpp`. For API v3+, `date` (from ledger close time) and `ctid` (computed from ledger seq, transaction index, and network ID) are explicitly added at the transaction-object level outside `tx_json`. Added required `CTID.h` and `NetworkIDService.h` includes.
- **`src/test/rpc/Transaction_test.cpp`**: Asserts `date`, `ledger_index`, `ctid` absent from `tx_json` in v3; asserts `date` present at result level in v3; present in `tx_json` in v2.
- **`src/test/rpc/AccountTx_test.cpp`**: Split `case 2`/`case 3` in `hasTxs` with assertions that `date` and `ctid` are absent from `tx_json` but present at the transaction-object level in v3.
- **`API-VERSION-3.md`**: Documents breaking change with correct scope (API v2 only, not v1, since v1 uses `tx` key not `tx_json`).

items.title: Dynamic MPT (XLS-94) + Confidential Transfers:
items.body:
Summary:
When an issuer dynamically updates a mutable field (e.g., MaxAmount or related flags) in an MPTokenIssuance object that has active confidential balances/transfers, the update can desynchronize the public OutstandingAmount / MaxAmount invariant from the confidential COA and version counters. This occurs especially under concurrent or partial-apply scenarios, allowing ZK proofs validated against the old state to succeed against the new state (or vice versa), breaking supply soundness.

Root Cause:
XLS-94 mutable update logic in MPTokenIssuanceSet (or related transactor) does not atomically reconcile with XLS-96 confidential state (encrypted balances, sfConfidentialBalanceVersion, split COA/inbox, ZK equality/range proofs). No (or insufficient) re-validation of pending/in-flight confidential proofs or version counters occurs on mutable field changes. The current commit's implementation of sfMutableFlags + confidential hooks leaves a TOCTOU-style window.

Internal Pre-condition:  MPTokenIssuance object created with one or more fields marked mutable (sfMutableFlags set).  
Active confidential balances exist (holders with encrypted COA via EC-ElGamal + ZK proofs).  
OutstandingAmount ≤ MaxAmount invariant is enforced publicly, but confidential enforcement relies on proofs + version counters.  
Amendments for DynamicMPT + ConfidentialTransfer enabled.

External Pre-condition:  Attacker (or colluding issuer) can trigger MPTokenIssuanceSet on the mutable issuance (issuer-controlled, or via delegated/sponsored path if combined with other features).  
Confidential transfers have occurred (valid ZK proofs already submitted against prior MaxAmount).

Attack Path:  Issuer creates MPT issuance with MaxAmount (or key flags) marked mutable.  
Holders perform confidential transfers/sends, validating ZK proofs against current MaxAmount / OA.  
Issuer submits MPTokenIssuanceSet to lower MaxAmount (or change a mutable flag affecting supply rules) while some confidential operations or proofs are in flight or recently validated.  
(Optional amplifier) Wrap the update in a Batch inner with a failing later inner for partial apply, or combine with sponsored path.  
Replay a previously valid ZK proof (or submit new confidential send) against the updated issuance → proof passes validation but breaks the effective supply invariant (COA now exceeds new MaxAmount without detection, or underflow/overflow edges).

Impact:  Supply invariant violation: Confidential value can effectively exceed the (new) MaxAmount or violate other mutable constraints, leading to hidden inflation or deflation of institutional/privacy tokens.  
ZK replay or stale-proof acceptance, undermining the soundness of confidential transfers.  
Affects high-value use cases (regulated RWAs, institutional privacy rails). Could lead to undetected over-issuance or locked/unspendable confidential balances.  
Unlocks the Dynamic MPT and Confidential Transfers for MPT feature pools (potentially more if combined with Batch/Sponsored). High severity due to core accounting soundness risk.

Proof of Concept (Coded skeleton — executable via public JSON-RPC on local contest node once amendments enabled):  Setup (run first):  Issuer submits MPTokenIssuanceCreate with mutable MaxAmount (set sfMutableFlags appropriately per XLS-94).  
Fund holder accounts and perform initial confidential transfers to establish encrypted balances and version counters (use mpt-crypto tool for generating valid ZK proofs).

Attack Sequence:  Perform several ConfidentialMPTSend / Convert txs (ZK proofs validated against original MaxAmount).  
Issuer submits MPTokenIssuanceSet to reduce MaxAmount (or toggle mutable flag affecting enforcement).  
Immediately attempt to replay/submit a prior valid ZK proof or new confidential operation.

Example MPTokenIssuanceSet JSON skeleton:
{
  "TransactionType": "MPTokenIssuanceSet",
  "Account": "issuer_raddress",
  "MPTokenIssuanceID": "issuance_id_from_ledger",
  "MaxAmount": "reduced_value",   // mutable field update
  // other mutable fields as applicable
  "Flags": 0
}

Observe via ledger_entry on the MPTokenIssuance and holder MPToken objects:  Public OutstandingAmount vs new MaxAmount.  
Confidential fields (sfConfidentialBalanceVersion, COA components) — check for desync or successful replay of old proof.

Expected vs Actual (to be confirmed on testnet): Version counter or COA not properly invalidated/reconciled after mutable update → invariant broken (e.g., effective COA > new MaxAmount without tec error).

Mitigation:  Make MPTokenIssuanceSet on mutable fields atomic with full re-validation/invalidation of all active confidential balances and pending ZK proofs (e.g., force version counter bump across holders or require issuer-mediated re-proof).  
Add explicit invariant checks in the update transactor: ensure new MaxAmount ≥ current effective COA (public + confidential-enforced).  
Introduce a grace period or locking mechanism for mutable changes when confidential activity is detected.  
Align mutable flag semantics strictly with confidential immutability rules for consistency.

## High Level Overview of Change

Add support for `DomainID` to existing transactions `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` and `MPTokenIssuanceSet` 

<!--
Please include a summary of the changes.
This may be a direct input to the release notes.
If too broad, please consider splitting into multiple PRs.
If a relevant task or issue, please link it here.
-->

### Context of Change

In #5224 we added `DomainID` as an access control mechanism for `SingleAssetVault`. The actual implementation of this feature lies in `MPToken` and `MPTokenIssuance`, hence it makes sense to enable the use of `DomainID` also in `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` and `MPTokenIssuanceSet`, following same rules as in Vault:

* `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` and `MPTokenIssuanceSet` can only set `DomainID` if flag `MPTRequireAuth` is set
* `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` requires that `DomainID` be a non-zero, uint256 number
* `MPTokenIssuanceSet` allows `DomainID` to be zero (or empty) in which case it will remove `DomainID` from the `MPTokenIssuance` object

The change is amendment-gated by `SingleAssetVault`.

This is a non-breaking change because `SingleAssetVault` amendment is `Supported::no`, i.e. at this moment considered a work in progress, which cannot be enabled on the network.

items.body:

-->

## High Level Overview of Change
Add the Following Invariants to Confidential MPT: 

- Regular MPToken balance change (±X) == COA change (∓X) with same magnitude
- Cannot delete MPToken with non-zero confidential state:
- Cannot delete if sfIssuerEncryptedBalance exists 
- Cannot delete if sfConfidentialBalanceInboxand  sfConfidentialBalanceSpending exist

Privacy flag consistency:
- MPToken can only have encrypted fields if lsfMPTCanPrivacy is set on issuance
- If issuance doesn't have privacy enabled, no MPToken should have encrypted balances

Encrypted field existence consistency:
- If sfConfidentialBalanceSpending/sfConfidentialBalanceInbox exists, then sfIssuerEncryptedBalance must also exist (and vice versa)
- Confidential outstanding cannot exceed total outstanding
- Verifies sfConfidentialBalanceVersion is changed whenever sfConfidentialBalanceSpending is modified on an MPToken.

The base branch is `master`. This PR branch will be pushed directly to `release` and `master` (not squashed or rebased, and not using the GitHub UI).
# Release Notes

![XRP](docs/images/xrp-text-mark-black-small@2x.png)
This document contains the notes for the release `2.6.0` of `rippled` , the reference server implementation of the XRP Ledger protocol. To learn more about how to build, run or update a `rippled` server, visit https://xrpl.org/install-rippled.html

This release adds new features and bug fixes.

## [2.6.0] - 2025-08-27

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
- Change log to debug level for AMM offer retrieval and IOU payment check (#5686) by @intelliot
- Add -Wno-deprecated-declarations for Clang only (#5680) by @bthomee
- Improve logging of the reason to refuse a peer connection (#5664) by @Tapanito
- Make test suite names match the directory name (#5597) by @Afformativ
- Don't flag consensus as stalled prematurely (#5627) by @ximinez
- VaultWithdraw destination account bugfix (#5572) by @Bronek
- Add allowTrustLineLocking flag for account_info (#5525) by @dangell7
- Link with boost libraries explicitly (#5546) by @mathbunnyru
- Crash when trace-logging in tests (#5529) by @mvadari
- Crash in Slot::deletePeer (#5635) by @Bronek
- Clang-format CI job (#5598) by @Bronek
- macOS runner (#5585) by @a1q123456

### 🚀 Features

- Include `network_id` in validations and subscription stream responses (#5579) by @ckeshava
- Add support for `DomainID` in `MPTokenIssuance` transactions (#5509) by @Bronek
- Add MPT related txns into issuer's account history  (#5530) by @shawnxie999
- Add nftoken_id, nftoken_ids, offer_id to meta for transaction stream (#5230) by @tequdev

### 💼 Other

- Set version to 2.6.0 by @legleux
- Set version to 2.6.0-rc3 by @ximinez
- Set version to 2.6.0-rc2 by @legleux
- Update .git-blame-ignore-revs for #5657 (#5675) by @intelliot
- Fix BUILD.md instruction (#5676) by @Bronek
- Set version to 2.6.0-rc1 by @legleux
- Switch Conan 1 commands to Conan 2 and fix credentials (#5655) by @bthomee
- Upload Conan dependencies upon merge into develop (#5654) by @bthomee
- Build options cleanup (#5581) by @Bronek
- Updates Conan dependencies: Boost 1.86 (#5264) by @bthomee
- Update rocksdb (#5568) by @bthomee
- Switch instrumentation workflow to use dependencies (#5607) by @Bronek
- Remove the type filter from "ledger" RPC command (#4934) by @ckeshava
- Retire Flow Cross amendment (#5562) by @vvysokikh1
- Downgrade required CMake version for Antithesis SDK (#5548) by @Bronek
- Remove OwnerPaysFee as it's never fully supported (#5435) by @a1q123456
- Removes release notes from codebase (#5508) by @bthomee

### 🚜 Refactor

- Decouple CredentialHelpers from xrpld/app/tx (#5487) by @a1q123456
- Add XRPL_ABANDON and use it to abandon OwnerPaysFee (#5510) by @a1q123456
- Remove obsolete owner pays fee feature and XRPL_ABANDON stanza (#5550) by @a1q123456
- Restructure beast::rngfill (#5563) by @lmaisons
- Remove external libraries as they are hosted in our Conan Center Index fork (#5643) by @bthomee
- Decouple ledger from xrpld/app (#5492) by @a1q123456
- Makes HashRouter flags more type-safe (#5371) by @vlntb
- Change boost::shared_mutex to std::shared_mutex (#5576) by @Tapanito
- Update date, libarchive, nudb, openssl, sqlite3, xxhash packages (#5567) by @bthomee

### 📚 Documentation

- Updates list of maintainers and reviewers (#5687) by @bthomee
- Update BUILD.md for Conan 2 (#5478) by @Bronek
- Set up developer environment with specific XCode version (#5645) by @dangell7

### ⚡ Performance
- Revert ["perf: Move mutex to the partition level](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/pull/5486)" @ximinez 
- Optimize hash performance by avoiding allocating hash state object (#5469) by @a1q123456
- Move mutex to the partition level (#5486) by @vlntb

### 🧪 Testing

- Run unit tests regardless of 'Supported' amendment status (#5537) by @vvysokikh1
- Remove circular jtx.h dependencies (#5544) by @Bronek
- switch some unit tests to doctest (#5383) by @vvysokikh1

### ⚙️ Miscellaneous Tasks

- Run prettier on all files (#5657) by @mvadari

items.title: Support canonical ledger entry names in ledger/ledger_data/account_objects "type" field.

labels.name: Good First Issue
labels.description: Great issue for a new contributor

labels.name: Feature Request
labels.description: Used to indicate requests to add new features

items.body:
## Summary
The ledger, ledger_data , and account_objects methods accept a `type` field to filter the results to specific types of ledger entries. The values you pass in aren't always possible to determine from the entries' canonical JSON names so it's kind of a guessing game.

Since all of these methods are returning raw/canonical ledger entries anyway it would make more sense if the `type` field of these requests matched the canonical names as they appear in the `LedgerEntryType` field. Maybe for convenience they could be case-insensitive.

## Motivation

Would _you_ be able to guess all of the short names in this table?
| Canonical Name | Short Name |
|---|---|
| `AccountRoot` | `account` 😉 |
| `Amendments` | `amendments` |
| `Check` | `check` |
| `DepositPreauth` | `deposit_preauth` |
| `DirectoryNode` | `directory` 😩 |
| `Escrow` | `escrow` |
| `FeeSettings` | `fee` 😮  |
| `LedgerHashes` | `hashes` 😑 |
| `NegativeUNL` | (No short name defined—can't filter by this type.) |
| `NFTokenOffer` | `nft_offer` 🤔 |
| `NFTokenPage` | `nft_page` 🆕 |
| `Offer` | `offer` |
| `PayChannel` | `payment_channel` 😅 |
| `RippleState` | `state` 😓 |
| `SignerList` | `signer_list` |
| `Ticket` | `ticket` |

(Emoji are not part of the names, I just added them as reactions to point out the less obvious ones.)

These short names also have to be manually added to the API methods whenever new types of ledger objects are implemented.

## Solution
Modify these APIs (and any others that have a similar field, though I can't think of them offhand) so that `type` accepts the canonical name, case-insensitive. For backwards compatibility, continue to also support the existing short names (but mark them deprecated in the documentation).

Preferably, also do it in such a way that when someone develops a new ledger entry type, these methods support filtering on the new type using the canonical name with no new/additional code to the methods.

## Relevant Source Code
https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/ebbf4b64a57d2673d54a6b25def7726601d99bf9/src/ripple/rpc/impl/RPCHelpers.cpp#L894
